items.title: A statement becomes a description

states.label: A whole statement
states.note: The describing verb is the verb of the sentence.

states.label: Inside a noun phrase
states.note: The same verb follows the noun and says which car is meant.

items.caption: The describing word keeps its shape and remains a verb. Its position changes what the whole expression does.

items.title: The describing verb has number too
items.caption: The article disappears for the particular plural, and the describing verb takes its plural form. This is the agreement pattern taught for the noun as the verb’s single participant.

items.title: What fills the describing slot?

bins.label: A verb and a bare noun
A verb with a place phrase

items.why: The one built word stands as the describing verb.
The word *tino* names a body and *leaga* describes its quality.
The verb *fai* has the bare noun *umu* after it.

items.sm: le pasi alu ʻi le nuʻu
items.en: the bus going to the village
items.why: The verb *alu* carries the whole place phrase *ʻi le nuʻu* in the describing slot.

items.intro: Choose the kind of description after the noun.

items.title: The describing word comes after
items.intro: Tap the words to build the Sāmoan for each English. One word on offer does not belong.

items.why: The action verb *tagi* leads, and the describing verb *mālosi* follows it to say how the crying was done.
*Lelei* does the describing job after the action verb *siva*: danced, and danced well.
Three parts in a fixed order: the article *le*, the name of the thing *taʻavale*, then the describing verb *uliuli*.
The verb-and-noun compound *fai umu* works as one describing verb, and it stands behind the noun it describes.

items.en: the bus going to the village
items.sm: le pasi alu ʻi le nuʻu
items.why: The describing verb *alu* carries its place phrase *ʻi le nuʻu* behind it, and the whole of it stands in the one position after *le pasi*.

items.title: Learn the meanings of the built words
items.caption: Each built word has its own meaning. The chapter says to learn them word by word, rather than translate every one as difficult or easy.
